findings.message: e2e/conversation-practice.spec.ts's AC2 test ("a fake-mic pass reply drives a real pass verdict") had debug instrumentation left in the working tree: page.on('console'/'pageerror'/'requestfailed'/'response') listeners and four console.log(...) dumps of page.locator('main').innerText() interleaved with the real assertions. This was uncommitted scratch left over from diagnosing a flaky run (matches the round's diff, which was 100% additions of this instrumentation) — the committed HEAD state of the file never had it. Left in place it would spam CI logs every run and, worse, risked being committed by a later `git add -A`, permanently coupling the test to log-noise nobody reads. Removed all of it; `git diff HEAD` on the file is now empty (it matches HEAD exactly), so there is nothing new to commit for this file — the working tree is simply back to the last real commit's content.
